bug_semantics: When LiquidJS renders attacker-controlled template source with memoryLimit enabled, evalRangeToken meters a range as high - low + 1. A reverse range such as (100000000..1) therefore passes a large negative count to Limiter.use(); the vulnerable limiter accepts it and subtracts it from its cumulative base. Later positive allocations then satisfy base + count <= limit despite exceeding the configured budget. Repeated append operations can build a 134217728-character V8 cons-string, and replace forces flattening into a contiguous buffer, producing an uncatchable V8 fatal error and process-wide denial of service.
flaw_origin: Commit 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 attempted to fix unmetered ranges in for tags by adding exactly ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1) to evalRangeToken, but assumed low <= high. Its direct parent already had the generic Limiter, whose signed accumulator did not reject negative counts, but did not meter ranges and therefore lacked this reverse-range counter-poisoning path. The BIC is the smallest commit in which the advisory's signed range charge and permissive limiter coexist; it is a direct one-parent change, not a move, refactor, revert, release commit, or squash aggregate.
ai_marker: Absent. `git cat-file -p 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0` shows author and committer `Harttle <yangjvn@126.com>`, one parent, subject `fix: memoryLimit doesn't work in for tag, #776`, and no message body, Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, or other AI trailer.
evidence: The assigned GitHub advisory bundle for GHSA-9r5m-9576-7f6x/CVE-2026-33285 identifies `src/render/expression.ts` computing `high - low + 1`, `src/util/limiter.ts` accumulating the negative value, the reverse-range/append/replace attack chain, and advisory fix reference 95ddefc056a11a44d9e753fd47a39db2c241e578.

In the validated clone, `git log --all --reverse -S'ctx.memoryLimit.use' -- src/render/expression.ts` first adds the range charge at 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0. Independently, `git log -L '/ctx\.memoryLimit\.use/,+1':src/render/expression.ts 1b85fdaa9c535021f7030a239a64003af26d31b5` attributes the exact vulnerable line solely to that commit.

`git show 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0` shows the one-line source addition `ctx.memoryLimit.use(high - low + 1)` plus an ascending-range regression test `(1..1000000000)`; the arithmetic's reverse-range case was not handled. `git cat-file -p` gives its sole parent as d61855bf725a6deba203201357f7455f6f9b4a32.

Direct parent verification: `git show d61855bf725a6deba203201357f7455f6f9b4a32:src/render/expression.ts` shows evalRangeToken evaluating low/high and immediately returning `range(+low, +high + 1)` with no memoryLimit.use call. The same parent's `src/util/limiter.ts` has a signed `base`, converts count with toNumber, checks only the upper bound, and then adds count; thus the latent permissive accumulator existed, but the advisory's reverse-range negative-input edge did not.

Antecedent history distinguishes the BIC from the latent helper: e443068cb9281883ff0fe9f755a15f52ada4e7e2 (`feat: DoS prevention, #250`) introduced Limiter and memoryLimit in 2024-07, while 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 later introduced the exact reverse-range charge in 2024-12. The latter is the first commit containing the complete reported mechanism.

`git show 95ddefc056a11a44d9e753fd47a39db2c241e578` shows the direct fix changing Limiter.use and Limiter.check to act only when `+count > 0`, preventing reverse ranges from reducing the accumulated base. The fix has parent 1b85fdaa9c535021f7030a239a64003af26d31b5 and changes only `src/util/limiter.ts`.

Tag boundary: `git diff v10.19.0 v10.19.1 -- src/render/expression.ts` is exactly the vulnerable range-charge addition, and `git tag --contains 2af297f81ac465feb3277ba7b92f7236409370b0 --sort=version:refname` starts at v10.19.1. Thus the reverse-range mechanism is absent in v10.19.0 and first released in v10.19.1.

Fix boundary: `git tag --contains 95ddefc056a11a44d9e753fd47a39db2c241e578 --sort=version:refname` starts at v10.25.1; `git diff v10.25.0 v10.25.1 -- src/util/limiter.ts` is the positive-count guard, and the v10.25.1 changelog names 95ddefc as `mem limiter for invalid ranges`. Repository trees show v10.25.0 still has the vulnerable range charge, the signed accumulating limiter, and the public memoryLimit option, so the actual Git release boundary is affected v10.19.1 through v10.25.0 and fixed v10.25.1. This corrects the advisory bundle's narrower `<= 10.24.0` metadata, which is contradicted by the v10.25.0 tree.

reasoning: The security regression begins with the direct range-metering change, not with a later move or the 2026 limiter fix: the immediate parent cannot send a reverse-range-derived negative count, while the BIC can. The generic limiter weakness explains why the new signed charge becomes exploitable, and the positive-count guard in 95ddefc closes that causal chain.
